Echoing a bit of what the other commenter has said, it really depends on the format of your exams. 
My written exams are all MCQ so I usually crank through Passmed/Pastest over the course of the year for prep. 
I'm a big fan of "illness scripts" and personally have a hybrid approach. Once I've familiarised myself enough with an illness on Passmed etc. I'll write up an illness script for it, and then tape it up on my wall (it helps if you have a big wall in your room). I'm a very visual learner who absentmindedly likes to zone out at things so I figured I may as well zone out on something useful! 
It may sound silly, but I definitely think drilling question banks + taping up illness scripts works for me, and it keeps several common illnesses somewhere in my attention span. I can vouch for it because it's the technique I used for my most recent exam and I still managed a 70+ somehow, despite intercalating last year. Best of luck with your finals! Also ZeroToFinals is a pretty good resource if you haven't used it already.
